cues.speaker: ROSIE
cues.text: Colin, I’m really struggling to think of a topic for our human geography assignment.

cues.speaker: COLIN
cues.text: Me too, Rosie. I’ll tell you what, let’s think about the different aspects of human geography and see if we can narrow the topic down a bit to help us decide.

cues.speaker: ROSIE
cues.text: OK. So one aspect is population. That would be all about population density and migration and so on. Lots of facts and statistics. Maybe a bit boring?

cues.speaker: COLIN
cues.text: Yeah, but quite straightforward to find on the internet.

cues.speaker: ROSIE
cues.text: Suppose so.

cues.speaker: ROSIE
cues.text: How about health?

cues.speaker: ROSIE
cues.text: I’d never thought about the links between that and geography until Professor Lee gave us that lecture on cholera.

cues.speaker: ROSIE
cues.text: How in the 19th century, a physician used street plans and plans of water supplies to find the source of a cholera epidemic.

cues.speaker: COLIN
cues.text: Yes, fascinating, wasn’t it? Or we could do something more general like economies

cues.speaker: ROSIE
cues.text: So how financial and commercial factors are linked to the physical environment

cues.speaker: COLIN
cues.text: Yeah

cues.speaker: ROSIE
cues.text: I thought that had been taken off the syllabus for this year

cues.speaker: COLIN
cues.text: Has it

cues.speaker: ROSIE
cues.text: I not sure but it might be best to avoid it

cues.speaker: COLIN
cues.text: OK. Maybe we could do something on culture. We had that lecture about culture and geography last week.

cues.speaker: ROSIE
cues.text: I didn’t get much out of that. It was all so general and the lecturer didn’t give any useful examples.

cues.speaker: COLIN
cues.text: Yeah, I hardly took any notes. It didn’t seem worth it.

cues.speaker: ROSIE
cues.text: Me neither.

cues.speaker: COLIN
cues.text: We could focus on poverty. That’s something that’s a global problem.

cues.speaker: ROSIE
cues.text: The trouble is, Dr Lee was saying, that you have to be careful with some of the figures relating to poverty. They’re sometimes deliberately manipulated.

cues.speaker: COLIN
cues.text: You mean the information gets changed for political reasons?

cues.speaker: ROSIE
cues.text: That sort of thing, yes.
Before you hear the rest of the discussion, you have some time to look at questions 26 to 30. you Now listen and answer questions 26 to 30.

cues.speaker: ROSIE
cues.text: So what are we going to do our assignment on?

cues.speaker: ROSIE
cues.text: I’ll tell you what.

cues.speaker: ROSIE
cues.text: One of the possibilities we have discussed is urbanisation and now over half the world population lives in cities.

cues.speaker: ROSIE
cues.text: That really important

cues.speaker: COLIN
cues.text: OK good idea Rosie Let do that

cues.speaker: ROSIE
cues.text: I love living in a big city but of course there are problems

cues.speaker: COLIN
cues.text: Things like theft and robbery?

cues.speaker: ROSIE
cues.text: Yes, but where I come from, that’s linked to another more serious issue, which is that a lot of people don’t have jobs.

cues.speaker: ROSIE
cues.text: That’s getting worse and worse.

cues.speaker: ROSIE
cues.text: And we also still have quite a lot of people who are homeless, though that’s not quite so bad as it was.

cues.speaker: COLIN
cues.text: It would be nice to talk about some positive developments, like some of the new developments on the outskirts of cities.

cues.speaker: ROSIE
cues.text: Yeah, they’ve opened some massive new shopping centres outside my city.

cues.speaker: COLIN
cues.text: Yeah, the same with mine, but it means a lot of the shops in the city centre are closing down.

cues.speaker: COLIN
cues.text: But the outskirts are ideal for buildings that need a lot of space, like for conferences.

cues.speaker: COLIN
cues.text: They’ve opened a couple of big ones.

cues.speaker: ROSIE
cues.text: Yes, we’ve got some too. It’d be nicer to have more facilities for things like football too, but that’s not happening where I live.

cues.speaker: COLIN
cues.text: Same in my area.

cues.speaker: ROSIE
cues.text: We could include something about developing disused industrial sites. It seems like a good idea because you’re not doing any harm to the natural environment.

cues.speaker: COLIN
cues.text: Yeah, but aren’t the buildings architecturally significant?

cues.speaker: ROSIE
cues.text: Not really. And what people forget is that they often used quite dangerous materials, chemicals

cues.speaker: ROSIE
cues.text: and things, which haven’t been properly cleared away, so the whole site has to be made safe.

cues.speaker: COLIN
cues.text: Hmm, that can’t be cheap. And I bet it’s often not budgeted for.

cues.speaker: ROSIE
cues.text: You’re right.

cues.speaker: COLIN
cues.text: Have you read about Masdar City?

cues.speaker: ROSIE
cues.text: In Abu Dhabi? Yes. It was designed to be a green city, wasn’t it? That might be a good example of a city which set out to depend entirely on renewable energy.

cues.speaker: COLIN
cues.text: Yes we should say something about that It was designed to be totally pedestrianised too wasn’t it with the transport underground

cues.speaker: ROSIE
cues.text: Yes and they had big plans for recycling to reduce waste to the lowest possible level But let’s stick to talking about power sources.

cues.speaker: COLIN
cues.text: Then there’s that ecotown in England, Greenhill Abbotts.

cues.speaker: COLIN
cues.text: It set out to conform to the usual principles, sustainability and so on.

cues.speaker: COLIN
cues.text: A lot of people were against it at first.

cues.speaker: COLIN
cues.text: They said the plans were unrealistic.

cues.speaker: COLIN
cues.text: I’m not sure how far they’ve got with it.

cues.speaker: COLIN
cues.text: I’ll check.

cues.speaker: ROSIE
cues.text: Right. So it looks as if we have a sort of plan.
